## Definition

Let $k,n\ge1$ be integers, let $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$, and let
$$
\Delta_k=\left\{p\in[0,1]^k:\sum_{i=1}^k p_i=1\right\}.
$$
On a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$, let $(\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^n$ be the discrete filtration generated by the complete histories through round $t$, with $\mathcal F_0$ trivial; a complete pre-action history records past reward vectors, actions, and observed rewards. A reward vector is either fixed in advance or a deterministic function of the complete pre-action history. Thus, at a finite horizon with finitely many arms, there are finitely many possible histories. Before action $A_t$ is drawn, the current reward vector $x_t=(x_{t,1},\ldots,x_{t,k})\in[0,1]^k$ and sampling distribution $P_t=(P_{t,1},\ldots,P_{t,k})\in\Delta_k$ are $\mathcal F_{t-1}$-measurable, and $P_{t,i}>0$ for every $i$. The finite-valued measurable action $A_t\in[k]$ has conditional law $\mathbb P(A_t=i\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=P_{t,i}$. The learner observes only $X_t=x_{t,A_t}$ and sets
$$
Y_t=1-X_t,\qquad y_{t,i}=1-x_{t,i},\qquad \widehat Y_{t,i}=\frac{\mathbf 1\{A_t=i\}Y_t}{P_{t,i}},\qquad \widehat X_{t,i}=1-\widehat Y_{t,i}.
$$
The quantity $\widehat Y_{t,i}$ is the importance-weighted loss estimate for arm $i$, and $\widehat X_{t,i}$ is its corresponding reward estimate. A fixed reward sequence is the oblivious case; allowing $x_t$ to depend on the history available before $A_t$ is drawn gives the non-anticipating past-adaptive case. In either case the current reward vector is chosen before the current action. For finite horizons and finite action histories generated by such a fixed or deterministic history-dependent sequence, all these estimates are finite and integrable.

## Statement

In the bandit importance-weighted estimator definition, fix a round $t$ and arm $i$, and write $p=P_{t,i}>0$ and $y=y_{t,i}$. Then
$$
\mathbb E[\widehat Y_{t,i}\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=y_{t,i},\qquad \mathbb E[\widehat Y_{t,i}^{2}\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=\frac{y_{t,i}^2}{P_{t,i}}.
$$
With conditional variance defined by $\operatorname{Var}(Z\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=\mathbb E[(Z-\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}])^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]$, one also has
$$
\operatorname{Var}(\widehat Y_{t,i}\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=\frac{y_{t,i}^2(1-P_{t,i})}{P_{t,i}}.
$$

## Definition

Let $k>1$ and $n\ge1$ be integers, and let $\eta>0$. Use the finite-arm bandit protocol with rewards in $[0,1]$ and conditional sampling as specified in the bandit importance-weighted estimator definition. Initialize $\widehat S_{0,i}=0$ for each $i\in[k]$. For rounds $t=1,\ldots,n$, perform the following operations:

1. Set
   $$
   P_{t,i}=\frac{\exp(\eta\widehat S_{t-1,i})}{\sum_{j=1}^k\exp(\eta\widehat S_{t-1,j})},\qquad i\in[k].
   $$
2. Draw a measurable finite-valued action $A_t$ with conditional probabilities $\mathbb P(A_t=i\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=P_{t,i}$, and observe only $X_t=x_{t,A_t}$.
3. Form the loss estimates $\widehat Y_{t,i}=\mathbf1\{A_t=i\}(1-X_t)/P_{t,i}$ and reward estimates $\widehat X_{t,i}=1-\widehat Y_{t,i}$ for every $i\in[k]$.
4. Update $\widehat S_{t,i}=\widehat S_{t-1,i}+\widehat X_{t,i}$ for every $i\in[k]$.

The output is $(P_t,A_t,X_t,\widehat X_t,\widehat Y_t)_{t=1}^n$ and $\widehat S_n$. These operations use exact real arithmetic. The procedure assumes a probability space carrying the stated measurable draws; it makes no probability-space construction claim. It is well-defined by induction: $\widehat S_{0,i}$ is finite; if the previous estimates are finite, every exponential weight is positive and finite, so the finite normalizing sum is positive and finite and $P_{t,i}>0$; then the observed loss estimate and update are finite. Normalizing the weights $\exp(\eta\widehat S_{t-1,i})$ is the exponential-weights step used by Hedge. Equivalently, since $\widehat S_{t-1,i}=(t-1)-\sum_{s<t}\widehat Y_{s,i}$, subtracting the common constant $t-1$ leaves the same probabilities as weights proportional to $\exp(-\eta\sum_{s<t}\widehat Y_{s,i})$.

## Statement

Let $n\ge1$ and $k>1$ be integers. Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in[0,1]^k$ be a reward sequence fixed before the learner's random choices, and run Exp3 with learning rate
$$
\eta=\sqrt{\frac{2\log k}{nk}}.
$$
Here $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
Write $X_t=x_{t,A_t}$ and define expected regret against the best fixed arm by
$$
R_n=\max_{i\in[k]}\sum_{t=1}^n x_{t,i}-\mathbb E\left[\sum_{t=1}^n X_t\right].
$$
Then
$$
R_n\le\sqrt{2nk\log k}.
$$

The same bound holds when each $x_t$ is a deterministic function of the complete history available before $A_t$ is drawn, provided $x_t\in[0,1]^k$. In that past-adaptive case define
$$
R_n^{\mathrm{past}}=\max_{i\in[k]}\mathbb E\left[\sum_{t=1}^n(x_{t,i}-X_t)\right],
$$
with the maximum outside the expectation; then $R_n^{\mathrm{past}}\le\sqrt{2nk\log k}$. This is an expected fixed-arm regret bound, not a high-probability bound, an expected in-hindsight maximum bound for random reward vectors, or a policy-regret bound for a reward rule that responds to the current action.

## Statement

Let $n\ge1$ and $k>1$ be integers. Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in[0,1]^k$ be a reward sequence fixed before the learner's random choices, and run Exp3 with learning rate
$$
\eta=\sqrt{\frac{2\log k}{nk}}.
$$
Here $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
Assume the run is on a probability space carrying the measurable, finite-valued actions with the conditional probabilities specified by Exp3; no probability-space construction is asserted. Every normalizing denominator is finite and positive, all estimates and cumulative estimates are finite, and the procedure completes its $n$ rounds. For every $t\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$ and $i\in[k]$,
$$
\widehat S_{t,i}=t-\sum_{s=1}^t\widehat Y_{s,i},
$$
where the sum is empty when $t=0$. Consequently, for every $t\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$,
$$
P_{t,i}=\frac{\exp(-\eta\sum_{s<t}\widehat Y_{s,i})}{\sum_{j=1}^k\exp(-\eta\sum_{s<t}\widehat Y_{s,j})},\qquad i\in[k].
$$
Write $X_t=x_{t,A_t}$ and define expected regret against the best fixed arm by
$$
R_n=\max_{i\in[k]}\sum_{t=1}^n x_{t,i}-\mathbb E\left[\sum_{t=1}^n X_t\right].
$$
Then
$$
R_n\le\sqrt{2nk\log k}.
$$

The same bound holds when each $x_t$ is a deterministic function of the complete history available before $A_t$ is drawn, provided $x_t\in[0,1]^k$. In that past-adaptive case define
$$
R_n^{\mathrm{past}}=\max_{i\in[k]}\mathbb E\left[\sum_{t=1}^n(x_{t,i}-X_t)\right],
$$
with the maximum outside the expectation; then $R_n^{\mathrm{past}}\le\sqrt{2nk\log k}$. This is an expected fixed-arm regret bound, not a high-probability bound, an expected in-hindsight maximum bound for random reward vectors, or a policy-regret bound for a reward rule that responds to the current action.
